title: Count Sub Islands
summary: Given two m x n binary matrices, grid1 and grid2, where 1's represent land and 0's represent water, count the number of islands in grid2 that are completely contained within any island in grid1.
statement: Given two m x n binary matrices, grid1 and grid2, where 1's represent land and 0's represent water, count the number of islands in grid2 that are completely contained within any island in grid1.
constraints: The two binary grids have identical dimensions up to 500 by 500.
Land connects only orthogonally; each grid2 island is one maximal connected land component.
Count a grid2 island only when every one of its cells is land in grid1.
hints: Treat each unvisited grid2 land cell as the start of one flood fill.
Traverse its entire component using the four orthogonal directions while remembering whether any cell lies over grid1 water.
Count the component only if that validity flag remains true; use an explicit stack to avoid recursion-depth failure on large grids.
Flood fill visits every grid2 island exactly once, and checking every visited cell is precisely the definition of complete containment.
editorial: Flood fill visits every grid2 island exactly once, and checking every visited cell is precisely the definition of complete containment.

tests.explanation: Three grid2 components lie entirely on grid1 land.
The connected grid2 island includes a cell over grid1 water, so it is not a sub-island.
